subtype: Parent or elder teaching a skill [Observer]
passage: Note by Chinmay, volunteer at the community workshop. Observed on Tuesday: Rajni was teaching a teenager to change a bicycle tyre. The tyre kept slipping. Rajni's hands twitched twice, and both times Rajni put them behind the back and asked, "What do you think is wrong?" It took the teenager eleven minutes, and fingers were pinched once. Rajni stepped in only when asked, and then showed just one move: lever on the opposite side. Then hands off again. The tyre held. The teenager said, "I did it," and was still grinning when Rajni handed over the pump. I will suggest we do this on more benches. - Chinmay

qa.q: How long did it take the teenager to change the tyre?
qa.a: It took the teenager eleven minutes.

qa.q: What was the teenager feeling at the end, and what shows it?
qa.a: Proud and delighted, shown by saying "I did it" and grinning.

qa.q: What did Rajni do when the teenager finally asked for help?
qa.a: Rajni showed just one move, the lever on the opposite side, and then stepped back again.

qa.q: What might Rajni have been feeling when Rajni's hands twitched twice?
qa.a: An urge to take over the task, along with the restraint to let the teenager struggle a little.

grounding: Shows an observer noticing an elder who lets a young learner struggle before giving one small hint.

subtype: Parent or elder teaching a skill [Observer]
passage: Sunday. Watched Irfan Chacha teach my cousin to hammer a nail properly in the balcony workshop. First nail bent. Second nail bent. My hands itched to say something, and I could tell Chacha's did too, but Chacha kept sipping tea instead. Third nail went in halfway, and my cousin said, "It's the way I hold it." Only then did Chacha say, "Try holding further down." Fourth nail went in straight. My cousin's face! I would have grabbed the hammer by the second nail. Note to self: when I teach, sip the tea. - Dhruv

qa.q: How many nails did the cousin hammer, and which one went in straight?
qa.a: The cousin hammered four nails, and the fourth went in straight.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling while watching the bent nails?
qa.a: Impatient and itching to step in, but impressed by Chacha's patience.

qa.q: What could Dhruv do next time when teaching?
qa.a: Stay quiet and wait for the learner to name the problem, then offer one small hint.

qa.q: Why might Irfan Chacha have waited for the cousin to say "It's the way I hold it"?
qa.a: Chacha let the cousin discover the problem first, so the tip to hold further down would make sense.

passage:
Zubin had come to Disha's village near Nashik for her sister's engagement. On the second morning, he sat on the verandah with his tea and watched Disha's grandmother teach her to make bhakri on the chulha.
Disha's first one tore. The second was thick in the middle. Aaji did not take the dough. She sat on her low stool and said only, "Wet your palm." Disha's face was pink with heat and irritation.
Zubin, who could not cook at all, wanted to shout suggestions. He bit his tongue.
The fourth bhakri was round but stuck to the pan. Disha looked at Aaji, pleading. Aaji leaned over, flicked a few drops of water on the pan, then sat back. "Now you."
The sixth one puffed up. Disha held it up on the tongs like a trophy. Aaji just nodded once. Zubin noticed Disha ate that one herself, slowly, smiling.

qa.q: What did Aaji say after the second bhakri?
qa.a: She said only, "Wet your palm."

qa.q: What was Zubin feeling as he watched Disha struggle?
qa.a: Zubin felt restless and eager to help, wanting to shout suggestions but biting his tongue.

qa.q: Which of Aaji's choices helped Disha most, and why?
qa.a: Aaji stepped in only once, briefly, then said "Now you," so Disha kept doing the work and earned the puffed-up bhakri herself.

qa.q: How does Disha feel when the sixth bhakri puffs up?
qa.a: Disha feels proud and delighted, holding it up like a trophy and eating it slowly, smiling.

grounding: An observer watches an elder let a young woman struggle with a skill and step in only a little, building skill and confidence.

subtype: Parent or elder teaching a skill [Observer]
passage:
From his porch in Curitiba, Ivan had a clear view of the street where Priscila's father was teaching her to drive his old manual car.
The car jerked forward and stalled. Then again. Priscila slapped the wheel. Ivan, who had learned to drive with his own father shouting, waited for the shouting to begin.
It didn't. Senhor Almeida sat with one arm out of the window. Ivan could hear him through the open window: "Slower on the clutch. Feel for the bite." Nothing else.
The car stalled a fourth time. Priscila put her face in her hands. Her father reached over, put his hand briefly over hers on the gearstick, showed her the movement once, and took his hand back.
On the sixth try, the car rolled smoothly to the corner. Priscila honked twice. Ivan found himself clapping on his porch, alone, and felt a small pang about his own lessons.

qa.q: How many times had the car stalled before Priscila's father showed her the movement?
qa.a: The car stalled a fourth time before he showed her.

qa.q: What did Ivan feel as he clapped alone on the porch?
qa.a: Ivan felt happy for Priscila and a small pang about his own lessons with a shouting father.

qa.q: What did Senhor Almeida do that other teachers could copy?
qa.a: He stayed calm, gave one short hint at a time, showed the movement once and then took his hand back so Priscila could try.

qa.q: How does Priscila feel on the sixth try?
qa.a: Priscila feels proud and happy, honking twice when the car rolls smoothly to the corner.

grounding: An observer sees a father let his daughter struggle a little while learning to drive, stepping in only briefly, which builds her skill.

passage:
Trisha was restocking thread at the community centre's Saturday tailoring class when she noticed the corner table. Lalremsiami, the oldest teacher there, sat beside a teenage boy, Deepu, who was fighting a jammed sewing machine. The thread had knotted under the plate. Trisha's hands itched; she knew the fix and half-rose from her stool.
Lalremsiami didn't move. She sipped her tea and asked only, "Where does the thread go after the needle?"
Deepu muttered, pulled the bobbin out, frowned, and put it back the wrong way. Trisha winced. Another minute passed.
"Look at the little arrow," Lalremsiami said, tapping the machine once.
Deepu turned the bobbin, rethreaded, and pressed the pedal. The needle ran clean. He grinned and sewed a whole seam without looking up.
Trisha sat back down, a little embarrassed at how fast she had wanted to grab it.

qa.q: What had gone wrong with Deepu's sewing machine?
qa.a: It was jammed; the thread had knotted under the plate.

qa.q: What was Trisha feeling as she watched Deepu struggle?
qa.a: Trisha felt restless and tense, itching to fix it herself, and afterwards a little embarrassed at how fast she had wanted to grab it.

qa.q: What small step did Lalremsiami use to help without taking over?
qa.a: She waited, asked one question, and only after Deepu had tried for a while gave a single hint by tapping the little arrow.

qa.q: How might Deepu feel after getting the machine running himself?
qa.a: Deepu likely felt proud and more confident; he grinned and sewed a whole seam after solving it with only small hints.

grounding: Shows an observer watching an elder let a young person struggle a little before offering a small hint.
